newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee ends firm despite late dlr demand.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee ends firm despite late dlr demand.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed firm despite late demand for dollars, as the local currency gained ground when the buyer of the U.S. unit moved out, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 57.23 to the dollar after opening at 57.28. The currency closed at 57.26 on Friday.
"The dollar fell back the moment a state bank, which was the main buyer, moved out," said a Deutsche Bank dealer.
There was no speculation to prop up the U.S. unit either, since today's cut of the statutory reserve left the market in no doubt that the Central Bank wanted to maintain rats low, he said.

The Central Bank said it was cutting the statutory requirement to 14 percent from 15 percent on local currency deposits, and removing a five percent reserve on foreign currency deposits placed abroad.

Dealers expect the new rules to have a significant impact on call rates. "Overnight call rates which closed at 12.5 percent today, should sink further because a cut in statutory reserves will release a few billions of rupees into the system," said a Commercial Bank dealer.
Some dealers expect the Central Bank's overnight repo rate now at 12 percent, to fall to 10 percent within the next month.
